plain_description: Garak protects your business by automatically stress-testing LLM applications for security vulnerabilities before attackers can exploit them. It probes for jailbreaks, data leaks, prompt injection, hallucination, and dozens of other failure modes in a single automated scan. The bottom line: catch weaknesses early with the industry-standard penetration testing toolkit for language models.
technical_description: Garak is a command-line framework for security probing of large language models. It configures a generator (the LLM under test), runs probes that generate adversarial inputs, and evaluates responses using specialized detectors. The architecture is plugin-based with categories for probes, detectors, generators, evaluators, and harnesses, each inheriting from base classes. Supported generator backends include Hugging Face Transformers (local and Inference API), OpenAI API, AWS Bedrock Converse API, Replicate, LiteLLM, GGUF/llama.cpp, GGML, Cohere, Groq, and NIM endpoints, plus arbitrary REST endpoints via configurable YAML. Probes cover prompt injection, encoding-based jailbreaks, DAN attacks, hallucination (snowball), toxicity, data leakage, malware generation, package hallucination, XSS, and adaptive attack generation. Results output as structured JSONL reports with per-probe failure rates. Runtime is Python 3.10+ with pip-based installation.
title: garak

body: Adding guardrails to large language models.
plain_description: Guardrails protects your AI applications by automatically validating everything your LLM sends and receives. It catches risky content like toxic language, competitor references, or formatting errors before they reach your users, and helps you extract structured data reliably from any LLM. The bottom line: deploy AI with confidence and built-in safety checks.
technical_description: Guardrails is a Python framework for adding input/output validation guards to LLM-powered applications. It provides a library of pre-built validators via Guardrails Hub that detect and mitigate risks such as toxic language, competitor mentions, regex mismatches, and structural violations. The framework supports structured data extraction from LLMs through Pydantic schema definitions, function calling for OpenAI-compatible models, and prompt optimization. Guardrails can run embedded within an application or as a standalone Flask/Gunicorn server exposing a REST API with OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
title: Guardrails

body: NeMo Guardrails is an open-source toolkit for easily adding programmable guardrails to LLM-based conversational systems.
plain_description: NeMo Guardrails keeps your AI chatbot safe, compliant, and on-brand by adding programmable safety rules between your app and the LLM. The big picture: it blocks jailbreaks, filters sensitive data, and enforces topic boundaries so your AI stays trustworthy. The bottom line: fewer compliance incidents and faster deployment of customer-facing AI.
technical_description: NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails is an open-source Python toolkit that adds programmable guardrails to LLM-based conversational applications. The library uses an async-first architecture with a Colang-based configuration language (v1.0 and v2.0) to define five guardrail types: input, dialog, retrieval, execution, and output rails. It integrates with multiple LLM providers including OpenAI, NVIDIA NIM, and Hugging Face models, and optionally supports LangChain as a runtime framework. Deployment options include direct Python library usage via pip or a standalone FastAPI server exposing an OpenAI-compatible REST API at /v1/chat/completions, also available as a Docker container. The built-in guardrails library includes jailbreak detection, injection detection, content safety, topic safety, fact-checking, hallucination detection, sensitive data masking, and integrations with ActiveFence, PolicyAI, and other third-party services.
title: NeMo Guardrails

body: An open-source framework for detecting, redacting, masking, and anonymizing sensitive data (PII) across text, images, and structured data. Supports NLP, pattern matching, and customizable pipelines.
plain_description: Presidio automatically detects and removes sensitive personal data (PII) from text and images, helping organizations meet data privacy compliance requirements. It works out of the box with built-in recognizers for credit card numbers, names, locations, and more, and can be customized for your specific needs. Deploy it in minutes via Python, Docker, or Kubernetes.
technical_description: Presidio is a modular Python framework for context-aware PII identification and de-identification in text and images. It provides an Analyzer leveraging Named Entity Recognition, regex patterns, rule-based logic, and checksum validation to detect sensitive entities, and an Anonymizer that applies redaction, masking, or replacement operators. The framework supports custom recognizers, external NLP model integration, and deployment as a containerized microservice via Docker or Kubernetes with PySpark support for distributed processing.
title: Presidio

body: Test your prompts, agents, and RAGs. Red teaming/pentesting/vulnerability scanning for AI. Compare performance of GPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, and more. Simple declarative configs with command line and CI/CD integration.  Used by OpenAI and Anthropic.
plain_description: Stop guessing and start shipping safer AI apps. Promptfoo lets you test prompts, compare LLM models side-by-side, and automatically scan for security vulnerabilities — all from your command line or CI/CD pipeline. Used by OpenAI and Anthropic, it replaces trial-and-error with data-driven decisions so you can build AI your users can trust.
technical_description: Promptfoo is an open-source CLI and library for automated evaluation and red-teaming of LLM applications. It supports testing prompts, models, and agents across multiple providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, Amazon Bedrock, and Ollama with declarative YAML/JSON configuration. The tool provides local execution of evaluations and vulnerability scanning, automated CI/CD integration through GitHub Actions, code scanning for LLM-related security issues, and a web-based results viewer. It runs as a Node.js application installable via npm, Homebrew, or pip, with support for custom scoring assertions, model-graded evaluations, and RAG pipeline testing.
title: Promptfoo

plain_description: Rebuff protects your AI applications from prompt injection attacks, one of the most critical security risks in generative AI. It uses four layers of defense to detect and block malicious inputs before they can compromise your system. The bottom line: add robust, self-hardening security to your LLM apps without building detection from scratch.
technical_description: Rebuff is a multi-layered prompt injection detection framework providing Python and JavaScript/TypeScript SDKs. It integrates with OpenAI's API for LLM-based detection, vector databases (Pinecone, Chroma) for attack signature learning and matching, and Supabase for server-side data management. The framework employs four detection layers: heuristic filtering, LLM-based prompt analysis, vector database attack recognition, and canary token leakage detection. A self-hosted Next.js server provides a REST API and playground UI, with configurable billing and credit tracking.
title: Rebuff
